title: I need some help trying to get more data to test my bot
author: TrustNo5460
selftext: I’ve been working on a sniper bot  for gold for about a month now just testing different filters and time frames and I’ve come up  with something that I think has potential, I am new at this as this is my first bot and I’ve been getting into trading for about 4 months now so any advice would be helpful I’m always willing to listen and learn, but I was playing around with risk yesterday and this was the result of my new sniping bot within a 2024-2025 gold market data. It is extreme risk involved and that I why I would like to gather more data for it to back test without overfitting. Lmk what I can change or test pls im still new

comments.author: JoshyyP00
comments.body: Data bento has really cheap data and 150 in credits to use for free

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
more data is the wrong fix for this one. you have one year of gold and a set of filters tuned on that same year, so any new year you add is the first real test and you only get to use it once. split what you have instead: tune on the first eight months, run the last four blind, and if the blind stretch looks like a different bot it was the filters, not the market. and cut the risk before anything else, a line that steep on one year means the sizing found the year, not the setup.

the blind run I do on my own desk, Quantradin, built it for exactly that step. site is quantradin.com, US equities and options only, so GLD rather than spot gold, paper only, no charge.

replies.author: TrustNo5460
replies.body: Thank you for the advice I will do this and see how the results differ you might be right and that the filters are tuned but how could I fix this problem, just more trial and error ?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: not trial and error, fewer knobs. every filter you tuned by eye is a guess about one year. drop them one at a time and rerun the blind four months; the ones you can remove without the blind stretch getting worse were never doing anything but fitting. what survives that is the bot.

replies.author: TrustNo5460
replies.body: Thank you I’ll will do this and see if the bot survives a longer period and multiple back tests with different versions cutting each filter I have that could be damaging the actual accuracy

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: one more thing: keep the four blind months untouched between versions. once you've peeked at them to choose a filter they're training data too.

comments.author: LuckOrEdge
comments.body: This looks cool and promising! But, as you've mentionned this is almost certainly overfitted. If you split your year of data for OOS analysis, make sure the amount of trades for the samples are statistically significant. If not... you'll need to purchase more data.
